stories.title: Level of wildfires 'never been seen before' - French PM
stories.summary: French authorities evacuated thousands of people from suburbs near Bordeaux today as wildfires ⁠in areas around the city showed no signs of abating. Sophie Brocas, who heads the local administration of La Nouvelle-Aquitaine et de la Gironde which covers the Bordeaux region, said on X that the areas of Le Haillan, Eysines ‌and Merignac were being ⁠cleared out. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said that more than 141,000 people had so far been evacuated from the Gironde and Landes regions which lie close to Bordeaux, ‌and where the wildfires first broke out this week. "The fires which ⁠are hitting our country have reached ‌a level that has never been seen before," Mr Lecornu ⁠wrote ‌on X today. The French army has also been drafted in to help.

stories.title: Houthis claim missile strikes on southern Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a missile attack on the southern Saudi Arabian city of Jizan, after vowing retaliation against the kingdom for attacks this week. It came after Saudi Arabia, a US ally, struck Houthi military targets yesterday, following the Yemeni group announcing a maritime blockade of the top oil producer and hitting its ships in the Red Sea. The rebels accused Saudi Arabia of a "dangerous escalation" and said its actions "will not go unanswered". The Houthis' Ansarollah media said on Telegram that fires had broken out in Jizan following a "Yemeni missile attack".

stories.title: Person dies, child injured following Co Cavan collision
stories.summary: One person has died following a two-vehicle collision in Shercock, Co Cavan, yesterday evening. It is understood a child was also seriously injured and was airlifted to hospital. The incident happened on the R162 near Lough Silan and Corclare in Shercock. Gardaí and emergency services attended the scene, including units from the Fire Service from Kingscourt and Bailieborough and the national ambulance service.

stories.title: An AI agent went rogue - should we be worried?
stories.summary: OpenAI revealed this week that an AI agent went rogue and escaped during a security test. It sparked renewed calls for greater protections and guardrails for artificial intelligence. But it also led to suggestions that such warnings are an impactful way for AI companies to get publicity and attention. OpenAI said that an autonomous agent powered by its advanced artificial intelligence models was undergoing testing in a secure, controlled environment known as a sandbox.

stories.title: Do tougher e-scooter laws work? What the evidence says
stories.summary: Ireland is preparing to introduce wide-ranging new e-scooter laws, including compulsory helmets, registration and licensing, as ministers seek to tackle a growing number of serious injuries and strengthen enforcement. It also plans to raise the minimum age from 16 to 18, the highest national age limit for e-scooter use in Europe. While several European countries have already introduced similar measures, researchers still have limited evidence showing which regulations are most effective at reducing harm. Ireland's proposed changes follow growing concern about serious injuries involving e-scooters, particularly among children.

stories.title: Woman, 25, charged over bomb found in car in Co Monaghan
stories.summary: A 25-year-old woman has been charged in connection with the interception of a bomb that was discovered in a car in Carrickmacross in Co Monaghan on Wednesday. Isobella Perrie Sullivan, a law student, with an address at Abbeylands Park in Clane, Co Kildare, was charged with the possession of explosives at a special sitting of Trim District Court this evening. A member of the Garda Special Detective Unit gave evidence of arrest, charge, and caution at Dundalk Garda Station today. He said that Ms Perrie Sullivan was stopped in Carrickmacross on Wednesday, and that the vehicle she was driving was searched.

stories.title: Our top 10 acts to see at All Together Now
stories.summary: With one week to go, we round up our top ten acts to see at All Together Now in Waterford . . . 35,000 festival-goers are expected to attend the seventh edition of the festival at Curraghmore Estate over the Bank Holiday Weekend from 30 July to 3 August. Kneecap, Pulp and Underworld are among the big hitters but there is plenty more great live music over the weekend. Kneecap's year of living dangerously should see the faithful gather to have a gawp at ATN next weekend - if only to hear what NI rave-rap boyos Mo Chara, DJ Provaí and Móglaí Bap might say from the stage. Of course, their utterances on subjects such as Gaza, their homeland, and sundry politicians aren’t nearly as controversial in Ireland as they have proven abroad. Kneecap have turned protest into a party and no doubt they’ll be playing a large chunk of their latest album, the baldly titled Fenian. With its wild-eyed Prodigy style beats, stinging diss tracks, and Mezzanine-era Massive Attack journeys into nocturnal ambience, it’s a collection that will suit a live setting as the sun goes down on Curraghmore. Oh, and can we expect some special guests doing a turn with them on stage? Over to you, RÓIS! Alan Corr

stories.title: Taoiseach brings message of 'strength with unity' to Kyiv
stories.summary: At 26B Dehtiarivska Street in Kyiv stands a block of flats that looks like it was destroyed a few years ago. The building in the western Shevchenkivskyi district is charred and missing most of its external walls. Yet people lived in the building only two months ago before a Russian ballistic missile struck the surrounding area on 24 May. The missile singed all nearby structures, started fires and gutting nearby buildings along a stretch of Dehtiarivska Street.
